column1: # The names of the 114 surahs.
# WHY A REGISTRY
# `surah` is the concept, and it has one dictionary entry saying what a surah
# is. These are its 114 members. A member is not a concept, so it does not get
# an entry — it gets a row, the way the twenty-eight letter names do.
# THESE NAMES ARE DERIVED
# Unlike the reciters in registries/qiraat.tsv, a surah name is a word, not a
# person. The derivation in tools/translit.py keeps its meaning, so `code` is
# derived from `arabic` by sections 4 to 8 and tools/check_registries.py
# re-derives every row. Four names are the exception, and they are exceptions
# for a stated reason: Taha, Yasin, Saad and Qaaf are named by the letters they
# open with, and the derivation reads those letters as a consonant cluster —
# `th`, `ys`, `s`, `q`, and `s` collides with the letter seen. They are written
# as they are said, like every other letter name, and the rows that do it are
# in data/established_spellings.tsv rather than hidden here.
# `display` follows the dictionary's convention and drops the leading article:
# `Fatihah`, not `Al-Fatihah`. The article-carrying form every reader also
# writes is in `alternative_spellings`, so both resolve to the same surah.
# THE OTHER NAMES ARE NAMES, NOT TRIVIA
# A surah is often known by more than one name — al-Tawbah is also Baraah, and
# al-Isra is also Bani Israil. `other_arabic_names` carries them because an
# application that only knows one of them cannot find a text that uses the
# other. It is not a complete list of every name a surah has ever been given.
# NOT HERE: whether a surah is Makki or Madani, and how many ayahs it has. The
# first is disputed for a good number of surahs and needs its own sourcing; the
# second is not one number but six, and belongs with registries/
# ayah_numbering.tsv when the per-surah counts are extracted. Neither is
# guessed at here.
# `ref` cites al-Itqan, al-Nawa al-Sabi Ashar, on the names of the Quran and of
# its surahs, as volume/page.
